description: A study of hydrogen covering its occurrence, laboratory preparation, physical and chemical properties, its role as a reducing agent, the pop sound test and its everyday uses.

mcq.questionText: Which metal is commonly reacted with dilute sulphuric acid to prepare hydrogen gas in the laboratory?
mcq.explanation: Zinc is moderately reactive and reacts with dilute acids to release hydrogen, while copper, gold and silver are too unreactive.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct test that confirms a gas collected in a test tube is hydrogen?

options.text: It burns with a squeaky pop sound when a lighted splint is applied

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen is confirmed by the squeaky pop sound it produces when a lighted splint is brought near it.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a correct physical property of hydrogen gas?

options.text: It is a colourless and odourless gas
It is a green poisonous gas
It is very soluble in water

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen is a colourless, odourless, tasteless gas that is lighter than air and only slightly soluble in water.

mcq.questionText: When hydrogen burns in oxygen, the product formed is:
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water (H2O), which is why hydrogen was once named the water-former.

mcq.questionText: Why is hydrogen gas usually collected over water during laboratory preparation?

options.text: Because it is very soluble in water
Because it is only slightly soluble in water
Because it reacts violently with water
Because it is denser than water

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen is only slightly soluble in water, so it can be conveniently collected over water by downward displacement of water.

mcq.questionText: When hydrogen is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, the colour change observed is from:
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen reduces black copper(II) oxide to reddish-brown copper metal, while itself being oxidised to water.

mcq.questionText: In the reaction between hydrogen and copper(II) oxide, hydrogen acts as a:
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from the metal oxide, so it is a reducing agent in such reactions.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is given off when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
mcq.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid, forming zinc chloride and releasing hydrogen gas.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is a major industrial use of hydrogen?

options.text: Manufacture of ammonia in the Haber process

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen combines with nitrogen in the Haber process to manufacture ammonia, an important raw material for fertilizers.

mcq.questionText: Why is hydrogen suitable for filling weather balloons?

options.text: Because it is heavier than air
Because it is lighter than air
Because it is poisonous to birds

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen has a very low density, making it lighter than air, so balloons filled with it can rise into the atmosphere.

mcq.questionText: In the universe, hydrogen mainly occurs:

options.text: As a free element making up most of the stars and the sun
Only locked in rocks as carbonates
As pure liquid pools on Earth's surface
Only combined with chlorine in sea water

mcq.explanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, occurring freely in stars including the sun, though on Earth it is mostly combined as in water.

mcq.questionText: During the laboratory preparation of hydrogen, a few drops of copper(II) sulphate solution are sometimes added to the zinc and acid mainly to:

options.text: Speed up the reaction by acting as a catalyst
Change the colour of the gas

mcq.explanation: A small amount of copper(II) sulphate acts as a catalyst that speeds up the otherwise slow reaction between pure zinc and dilute acid.

mcq.questionText: Which acid should NOT be used with zinc to prepare a clean supply of hydrogen because it acts as an oxidising agent and gives other gases?

options.text: Dilute sulphuric acid with a catalyst

mcq.explanation: Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent and reacts with metals to give oxides of nitrogen instead of hydrogen, so it is unsuitable.

mcq.questionText: The reaction in which hydrogen gas is added to vegetable oils to make solid fats such as margarine is called:
mcq.explanation: Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen to unsaturated oils, turning them into solid fats used to make margarine.

mcq.questionText: When collecting hydrogen by upward delivery (downward displacement of air), the gas jar is held mouth downwards because hydrogen is:
mcq.explanation: Because hydrogen is much less dense than air, it rises and collects at the top of an inverted gas jar held mouth downwards.

fib.questionText: The chemical symbol for the hydrogen atom is _____.
fib.explanation: The element hydrogen is represented by the symbol H, while the molecule of hydrogen gas is written as H2.

fib.questionText: Hydrogen gas is collected over _____ because it is only slightly soluble in it.
fib.explanation: Its low solubility in water allows hydrogen to be collected over water without much loss.

fib.questionText: When a lighted splint is brought near hydrogen, the gas burns with a squeaky _____ sound.
fib.explanation: The pop sound is the standard laboratory test that confirms the presence of hydrogen gas.

fib.questionText: Compared with air, hydrogen is _____ dense, which is why it makes balloons rise.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen is the least dense of all gases, making it lighter than air.

fib.questionText: The most abundant element in the whole universe is _____.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen makes up the greatest part of stars and the sun, making it the most abundant element in the universe.

fib.questionText: When hydrogen is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, the black solid is reduced to reddish-brown _____ metal.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from copper(II) oxide, leaving behind reddish-brown copper metal.

fib.questionText: Because it removes oxygen from metal oxides, hydrogen is described as a _____ agent.
fib.explanation: A substance that removes oxygen from another substance is called a reducing agent.

fib.questionText: When hydrogen burns in oxygen the only product formed is _____.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water, H2O, releasing a large amount of heat.

fib.questionText: In the Haber process hydrogen combines with nitrogen to manufacture _____.
fib.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) is produced industrially by combining hydrogen and nitrogen in the Haber process.

fib.questionText: The addition of hydrogen to liquid vegetable oils to make solid fats is called _____.
fib.explanation: Hydrogenation converts unsaturated oils into solid fats used in making margarine.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen is the lightest of all gases.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen has the lowest density of all gases, making it the lightest.
It is carbon dioxide, not hydrogen, that turns limewater milky; hydrogen gives a pop sound instead.

tf.questionText: Copper reacts readily with dilute hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen gas.
tf.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute acids.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen is a colourless and odourless gas.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen has no colour, smell or taste.

tf.questionText: A mixture of hydrogen and air can explode when ignited.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen is highly flammable and forms an explosive mixture with air or oxygen, which is the basis of the pop test.

tf.questionText: On Earth, most hydrogen exists as a free, uncombined gas in the atmosphere.
tf.explanation: On Earth hydrogen occurs mainly combined in compounds such as water and acids, not free in the air.

tf.questionText: When hydrogen reacts with a metal oxide, the hydrogen gains oxygen and is itself oxidised to water.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen takes oxygen from the metal oxide and forms water, so it is oxidised while reducing the oxide.

tf.questionText: Concentrated nitric acid is the best acid for preparing a pure supply of hydrogen with zinc.
tf.explanation: Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent and gives nitrogen oxides instead of hydrogen, so dilute sulphuric or hydrochloric acid is used.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen can be used as a fuel because it burns to release a large amount of energy.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen burns in oxygen to form water and releases much heat, making it a clean fuel.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen is very soluble in water.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen is only slightly soluble in water, which is why it can be collected over water.

summary.questionText: Most abundant element in the universe
summary.explanation: Hydrogen makes up most of the matter in stars and the sun.

summary.correctAnswer: Reacting a reactive metal such as zinc with a dilute acid
summary.explanation: Zinc plus dilute sulphuric or hydrochloric acid releases hydrogen gas.

summary.correctAnswer: It burns with a squeaky pop sound near a lighted splint

summary.questionText: Density of hydrogen compared to air
summary.correctAnswer: Hydrogen is much less dense than air (lighter than air)
summary.explanation: Its low density lets balloons filled with it rise.

summary.questionText: Product when hydrogen burns in oxygen
summary.explanation: Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water with much heat.

summary.questionText: Role of hydrogen with metal oxides
summary.correctAnswer: It acts as a reducing agent
summary.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from metal oxides, reducing them to the metal.
Low solubility allows collection over water.

summary.questionText: How to collect hydrogen by displacement of air
summary.correctAnswer: By downward displacement of air using a jar held mouth downwards
summary.explanation: Because hydrogen is lighter than air it rises into an inverted jar.

summary.questionText: Industrial use of hydrogen in fertilizer production
summary.correctAnswer: Manufacture of ammonia in the Haber process
summary.explanation: Hydrogen combines with nitrogen to make ammonia.

summary.questionText: Use of hydrogen in the food industry
summary.correctAnswer: Hydrogenation of oils to make margarine
summary.explanation: Adding hydrogen to liquid oils turns them into solid fats.

hoq.questionText: A student passes dry hydrogen over heated lead(II) oxide until the orange-yellow solid changes to a grey metallic bead, and water droplets form near the cool end of the tube. Which statement BEST explains these observations?

options.text: Hydrogen oxidises the lead oxide to lead while water is produced from the oxygen released
Hydrogen reduces lead(II) oxide to lead and is itself oxidised to water
The lead oxide acts as a reducing agent and turns hydrogen into water
Water forms because hydrogen dissolves in the lead oxide

hoq.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from lead(II) oxide, reducing it to grey lead metal, while the hydrogen combines with that oxygen to form water.

hoq.questionText: In a hydrogen preparation, pure zinc reacts very slowly with dilute sulphuric acid, but the reaction speeds up greatly after adding a few drops of copper(II) sulphate. The MOST correct reason is that:

options.text: Copper deposited on the zinc sets up tiny cells that act as a catalyst for the reaction
Copper(II) sulphate makes the acid more concentrated
Copper reacts with the acid to release extra hydrogen
Copper(II) sulphate increases the temperature of the acid permanently

hoq.explanation: The copper displaced onto the zinc surface forms many small galvanic cells that catalyse and speed up the release of hydrogen; copper itself does not react with the dilute acid.

hoq.questionText: A balloon filled with pure hydrogen rises and, when lit, burns quietly, but a balloon filled with a mixture of hydrogen and air explodes loudly with a bang. The BEST explanation for the difference is that:

options.text: Pure hydrogen is heavier and so burns more gently
Only the hydrogen-air mixture has oxygen evenly mixed throughout, so it burns extremely fast and explodes
Air prevents hydrogen from burning at all
Pure hydrogen contains no energy to release

hoq.explanation: When hydrogen is already mixed with oxygen from the air, combustion happens almost instantly throughout the mixture, producing the explosive bang, whereas pure hydrogen can only burn at its surface where it meets air.
